TERS Corruption

By: Liz Fish | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Unique Selling Point:
Ever since the TERS - the Temporary Employer / Employee Relief Scheme was established people have been complaining and crying foul. Last week Corruption Watch released a report into the extent of the corruption. The 1st payments/claims stared in April 2020 and extended to October last year. Mired in allegations of maladministration and corruption from the get-go, with the Auditor-General (AG) Tsakani Maluleke announced in November 2020 that 7 auditing firms would be appointed to track down the missing funds. The Corruption Watch report highlights 3 areas of corruption and Carte Blanche has been receiving numerous submissions since April last year that reflect them all. It’s a story close to our viewers hearts as both employers and employees are stuck in this mess at a time of extreme economic crisis. What should have been a life line for many has become a nightmare.

Summary:
The corruption has manifest from within TERS and from the public. Businesses owners have received payments for their employees but not paid the funds to the workers. A case in point is Honeydew Service station which claimed TERS for their workers, under both two different businesses Honeydew Service Station and Honeydew Quick Stop- double dipping. The workers could see on the TERS system that they had been paid out, but the business owner denied it. 18 people were fired when they wanted to know why they had not received their TERS paid out. To date they have not received their money and the owner will not fill in the UIF forms.
We have another case study where a restaurant owner was paid out R250 000 for her workers but still refuses to pay them, all have lost their jobs. Other employers and keeping half the money TERS paid out for themselves, which is also illegal. Some employers deducted UIF from their wages but had never registered them or paid the UIF and so they have no claim.


Further information:
The other element in the story is the major system failures- some people are still waiting for their funds from April last year. NESA - National Employers Association of SA tracks how extensive the problem is and 34% of the October claims have still not been paid out. 30% of Sept claims and 16 % of the claims from April have still not been settled.
Legal foreigners seemed to be the biggest victims of the system. They have lived and worked in South Africa and paid UIF for years but they not getting paid out. TERS keeps saying it’s a system error yet all their Home Affairs documents are loaded. Some received their payments in April but nothing since and now TERS says they not verifiable- it smacks of Xenophobia.
Then there is corruption within the system, funds are being syphoning off between the payout and the recipients bank account. Chantel Lacante who does payrolls for 150 companies says your queries are just unanswered. On the TERS system it reflects that she was paid R180 000 in June last year, she received R120 000 in her bank account, where did the R60 000 go? She is sent from pillar to post and 6 months later she is still short R60 000. A client of hers is short paid R8000 and a school in Umtata was missing R239 000, only when they started tagging Carte Blanche in the emails in January this year did the money finally get paid through.

Script:


Script: The Temporary Employer-Employee Relief Scheme known as "TERS", was instituted by the government in April 2020, to assist workers whose income have been affected by lockdown. TERS pay-outs came from UIF funds, and not the general fiscus. But, it’s been mired in allegations of corruption and system failures.
Script: The Auditor-General's report exposed that R41 million had been illegally paid out to Government employees. The SANDF, prisoners and even the dead, had cashed in. As a result, heads rolled last September and the top 5 UIF officials were suspended, and payouts temporarily halted. But by far the biggest complaint has been against employers. Francois Haarhoff was a site supervisor for Aerial and Satellite City.
Francois: So if TERS paid me out perhaps four thousand I only received four thousand, I didn't receive any salary
Script: TERS was designed to assist employees who were forced not to work, or work short time due to lockdown. The employer was obliged to pay for time worked, and TERS would cover their shortfall. It was not designed for employers to get the UIF, to pay their workers wages. Francois worked short time from May through to July, for which he was never paid
Mac: what you're saying to me is that the company was using the TERS payments to your full salary even though you were working .
Francois: Exactly. That's what happened.
Mac: Is that legal? Is that the right way to go?
Francois: I went to see an advocate and he advised me that it's totally wrong to do that.
Script: We took Francois case to the Acting UIF Commissioner, Marsha Bronkhorst
Mac: Could you just take us through almost like a dummy's guide of how TERS works for the employer and how it works for the employee?
Marsha: the employer will claim TERS if they have not been able to pay a salary to a worker because the worker was not working. Very important. If a worker was working, say, for two weeks out of four, the employer must pay the salary or wages for their two weeks and the TERS will top up the other two weeks. TERS was conceptualized to be an income replacement, not a subsidy to an employer for the salaries of the workers
Script: Francois claims Aerial and Satellite City owe him R40 500 for the days he worked, and approached a lawyer to help sort out the dispute. But instead he was dismissed and awaits the CCMA hearing.
Francois: I am so for I'm so far behind, I can't catch up on my payments at this stage.. I've got a small daughter that I need to pay school fees so it very hard for me
Script. Aerial and Satellite City dispute Marsha Bronkhosrt's interpretation of how TERS works. They said that TERS could be applied as the first payment towards the remuneration for work performed by an employee. They claimed that this interpretation of TERS was based on advice received from the UIF call centre in May 2020, and statements made by the president at the beginning of lockdown. Their records also differ on the amount of hours Francois worked, which will be settled at a CCMA hearing.
Script: All these people worked for Peter Wessels at his 3 filling stations, Honeydew, Blairgowrie and Sundowner in Johannesburg. Nompumelelo Dube was a petrol attendant at Honeydew Filling Station, and spoke for the group
Nompumelelo: We had to work either a one day, a week or two days a week.
Script: Earning R31.53 an hour, she only managed to bring in just over R2000 in April. As the sole breadwinner for her family, she was struggling to get by. In May she went online, and saw her TERS payment of R4027. Others did the same, and started asking their supervisor, when they could expect their TERS money
Nompumelo “Then in June, people started panicking. Now, because the other garage was totally closed which is in Blairgowrie so we decided we could only work a day or two days a week. So it was very, very difficult for us to make ends meet then we started communicating with other people from the other stations of which we found that nobody has been paid the money
Link: In April last year workers gathered here to find out from management what was happening with their TERS payments. They were accused of striking and intimidating the customers at the service station.
Script: At the confrontation in June, the financial manager said the reason no one was paid, was they hadn’t received TERS for everyone, so they felt it would be unfair to payout. Then then agreed to pay the TERS for those who they had received money for, but first subtracted their wages. Some only received only R54 of their R3000 TERS money
Marsha: If the employer had the benefit of an employee working for him for two weeks, three weeks, he must pay the wages, the TERS money pays the difference, the top up where there was no income by an employee.
Script. For their 4 businesses they claimed a total of R250 727 for April, the workers payslips show they received only R54 804 erroneously retaining the lion's share R195 921 for the company
Mac: If the employer's then keeping that money, what should happen to it
Marsha: It should be refunded to the UIF and with great speed, because we've started with our project to follow the money and all employers that are guilty of fraud, corrupt activities will be prosecuted
Script: Nompumelelo, along with 17 others were fired for striking illegally that day, and for 9 months, have struggled to get their UIF forms completed correctly by the company
Nomi: I would like to see the company paying for what they did wrong to people because they don't treat their workers properly
Script: Claiming ignorance of how the TERS system worked, despite every company having signed the memorandum of agreement, the financial officer did a complete about turn, when confronted with our evidence. In an email she wrote, “I will recalculate the TERS payment to the employees, and make the necessary adjustments and effect payments accordingly, for employees still employed. I will also refund the UIF where applicable, and pay those who are no longer working here. She sent us proof, a few days later
Link: Since April last year nearly R60 billion has been paid out in the Temporary Employee Relief Scheme or "TERS" to 4 and half million . But there is a huge backlog of pay-outs and system failures. Many are still waiting desperately for their first payment
Script: Marlie Kloppers represents 40 employees at a private school and has been struggling to get the first payout
Marlie The call centre of the UFI can't give you any information, any updates. So some of the staff members, their status says application processed on the 21st of December and has not been paid to date, and the rest of us applications are still not processed with no answers, nowhere to go. So what do we do
Script: The foreign employees, despite being legally in the country and contributing to UIF, the Ufiling system says they are not verified by either SARS or Home Affairs
Marlie: The person that's doing the finances, contacted TERS regarding the foreigners, and they said that the system says that the company had to fill in a letter and then they should go to the Department of Labor. When They they were treated very badly by the Department of Labor and they just said, listen, sorry, you guys are too late your company have to submit we can’t help you with TERS We can't help you with the TERS .
Marsha: The issue with foreign workers is indeed not so easy to resolve. You will recall the auditor general had an audit here and we were found wanting in terms of controls. Now for foreign workers can't be loaded on the TERS portal they have to be loaded on the Ufiling portal... Passport must be verified. So we found that we might want to verify it with home affairs because they the people who have the data base, they've got different databases of passports…... So we then said, let's then use also the passport numbers that is on the SARS database. ...they must pay the contributions to SARS. They must register their work on SARS as a contributor
Script: The TERS system is fully automated and if there is any minor error the system kicks it out. Like Marlie’s school, which was bought by a new owner after May, the system sees the same ID under two companies, but, she was never told this despite speaking to Bronkhorst herself. 9 months later some are still waiting for payment and the foreigners are still not processed
Link: With between 3 and 4 million people having lost their jobs over the last year the situation at the UIF officers is chronic. People cue here from early morning for days on end trying to get answers when their emails get nowhere
Precious Ndlovu “How long have you been coming here.Since last year October, Since last year October, And what do they keep saying, I must come back in 7 days, in 35 days I come here every month.
Script: Chantal La Cante handles the UIF and TERS payments for 50 companies and her experience, is pretty similar
Chantal: there is a lady that's was on maternity leave. We send in the documentation, it still says, on the system awaiting medical certificate and leave income.
Mac: And have those been provided.
Chantal: Yes, 20 times. what do you tell the client? Sorry, UIF is still waiting for this, but I supplied everything. Now, try harder than. Once you send the UI19 in for the normal client , then online support sends an e-mail. We received your email we'll get back to you.
Mac: And that's it, that's it . How much is this impacting your business?
Chantal: It's a lot because the people say once we receive payment, we'll pay you. I have 've lost three companies with that
Script. Marsha Bronkhurst admits the call centres are not equipped to answer any complex questions.
After the initial wave of fraud they stopped all payments and revamped the system which has caused endless problems and backlogs. Another major hold up, is if the UIF registration is even slightly different to the bank account name the system kicks it out.
Mac: One of the things the integration of a system where, you know, is SARS not speaking to home affairs. Home office is not speaking to the Labour Department, is UIF not speaking to the banks.
Marsha: Yeah, the Department of Public of Planning, Monitoring and evaluation in the presidency have started with a project of integrating all government systems. I think that is what we can learn from COVID is to see that government systems were fragmented and we going to roll out this project now. They busy with it
LINK: TERS has been extended to the end of March but many are asking if the overburden Department can cope with this new level of complexity
Maralie: I mean, this is a pandemic. I understand that. they were overwhelmed …..this has been almost a year now. So I feel that they could employ new people that could have done something

metadata.Unique Selling Point: Ever since the TERS - the Temporary Employer / Employee Relief Scheme was established people have been complaining and crying foul. Last week Corruption Watch released a report into the extent of the corruption. The 1st payments/claims stared in April 2020 and extended to October last year. Mired in allegations of maladministration and corruption from the get-go, with the Auditor-General (AG) Tsakani Maluleke announced in November 2020 that 7 auditing firms would be appointed to track down the missing funds. The Corruption Watch report highlights 3 areas of corruption and Carte Blanche has been receiving numerous submissions since April last year that reflect them all. It’s a story close to our viewers hearts as both employers and employees are stuck in this mess at a time of extreme economic crisis. What should have been a life line for many has become a nightmare.
metadata.Summary: The corruption has manifest from within TERS and from the public. Businesses owners have received payments for their employees but not paid the funds to the workers. A case in point is Honeydew Service station which claimed TERS for their workers, under both two different businesses Honeydew Service Station and Honeydew Quick Stop- double dipping. The workers could see on the TERS system that they had been paid out, but the business owner denied it. 18 people were fired when they wanted to know why they had not received their TERS paid out. To date they have not received their money and the owner will not fill in the UIF forms. We have another case study where a restaurant owner was paid out R250 000 for her workers but still refuses to pay them, all have lost their jobs. Other employers and keeping half the money TERS paid out for themselves, which is also illegal. Some employers deducted UIF from their wages but had never registered them or paid the UIF and so they have no claim.
metadata.Further information: The other element in the story is the major system failures- some people are still waiting for their funds from April last year. NESA - National Employers Association of SA tracks how extensive the problem is and 34% of the October claims have still not been paid out. 30% of Sept claims and 16 % of the claims from April have still not been settled. Legal foreigners seemed to be the biggest victims of the system. They have lived and worked in South Africa and paid UIF for years but they not getting paid out. TERS keeps saying it’s a system error yet all their Home Affairs documents are loaded. Some received their payments in April but nothing since and now TERS says they not verifiable- it smacks of Xenophobia. Then there is corruption within the system, funds are being syphoning off between the payout and the recipients bank account. Chantel Lacante who does payrolls for 150 companies says your queries are just unanswered. On the TERS system it reflects that she was paid R180 000 in June last year, she received R120 000 in her bank account, where did the R60 000 go? She is sent from pillar to post and 6 months later she is still short R60 000. A client of hers is short paid R8000 and a school in Umtata was missing R239 000, only when they started tagging Carte Blanche in the emails in January this year did the money finally get paid through.
